content:
- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows strong downward momentum; model fails to capture mean reversion in bearish phases.
- Forecast tends to lag in downward trends — true prices drop faster than model predicts, especially when sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative, model often fails to adjust downward quickly; correction needed within 3–5 days after sentiment dip.
- In bullish sentiment phases, model overreacts to recent highs, leading to overestimation in the 10–15 day horizon.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price declines during strong negative sentiment, especially when sentiment is below -0.40 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility — true outcomes show sharper swings than model suggests.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast window.
